tr-multifamily-content.note: Built for rental housing work, not repackaged generic business training. The documented design standard requires courses to be grounded in applicable law and regulation, recognized industry practice, internal and external subject matter experts, and legal counsel where risk warrants, using realistic property management scenarios. Every course moves through a defined pipeline: needs analysis, roadmap prioritization, development, quality assurance testing, senior leadership review and approval, then post-release monitoring. Two honest caveats. We do not publish a headline course count — catalog.gracehill.com is the source of truth for what exists today, and it is public with no login, so point a prospect at it rather than quoting a number. And compliance content is generally developed around federal law and not tailored to individual state or local requirements; the customer stays responsible for determining which requirements apply to them.

GHU Policy 3812 documents the pipeline: needs analysis, development, QA testing, senior leadership approval, post-deployment monitoring. GHU Policy 7003 states the federal-baseline rule.

tr-vendor-maintained.note: We watch legal and regulatory change and update the content, and the process is documented rather than asserted: ongoing monitoring, a bi-weekly review of developments that may affect the portfolio, periodic reviews with an annual review of priority compliance content, plus customer and field questions as an input. Each item resolves to one of five outcomes — Watch, Assess, Update or Develop, Escalate, or No Action — and higher-risk changes are approved by a Content leader with external counsel consulted when interpretation is needed. Two limits stated in the policy itself, and both are safer to say than to be caught on: monitoring is not a guarantee that every development produces an immediate content change, and it does not transfer the customer's compliance responsibility to Grace Hill. Monitoring is also scoped to topics in our portfolio, not to every federal, state and local requirement in existence.

The mechanism is visible in the monthly release notes, where courses are retired because the underlying law moved.
tr-vendor-maintained.lead: We watch legal and regulatory change and update the content, on a documented process rather than an assertion: ongoing monitoring, scheduled reviews, and every item resolved to a named outcome by a Content leader.
tr-vendor-maintained.limitLine: Monitoring is not a guarantee that every development produces an immediate content change, and it does not move the customer's compliance responsibility to Grace Hill. Say both before a prospect tests them.
tr-vendor-maintained.lookUp: Cadence, the five outcomes and the scope limits are in GHU Policy 3816. Monitoring covers topics in our portfolio, not every federal, state and local requirement in existence.

Analytics lets you compare performance across multiple locations to find leaders and laggards, and reports can be scheduled to inboxes or built custom and exported. Regions are configured in PerformanceHQ administration and can group locations by geography, ownership or operational oversight, with designated leaders who see region-level data. One boundary to know before you promise owner or asset-manager dashboards: the external-user capability that gives non-employees like owners and asset managers limited access is currently available to customers with the Resident Survey subscription, with other products noted as possible future additions.
rm-property-rollup.proof: Reputation Management | 8000 (AdminHQ) states access requires the Reputation User, Reputation Regional or Reputation Portfolio role and that the role determines which locations the user can access; describes the Home dashboard Executive Summary across all locations, Competition against local competitors, and Improving vs. Declining Locations; and describes Analytics & Reporting including the LBV Score benchmark combining reviews, social media activity, online listings and search rankings versus local competitors, Location comparison across multiple properties, Task Reports, scheduled Email Reports and Custom Reports / Query Builder with export. Manage Regions | 2091 (AdminHQ) documents creating regions to group locations by geography, ownership, portfolio structure or operational oversight, with Leaders who can view region-level data and a note that access and capabilities related to regions may vary by product and role. Manage External Users | 2068 (AdminHQ) states external-user management — for asset managers, owners and third-party consultants — is currently available to customers with the Resident Survey product subscription, with support for additional products possible in future releases.
rm-property-rollup.statedLimit: Region-level access and capabilities vary by product and role (AdminHQ 2091), and external-user access for owners and asset managers is currently limited to customers with the Resident Survey subscription (AdminHQ 2068).

ms-human-shoppers.note: Yes. Grace Hill shops are performed by real people — a national pool of independent contractors, not software listening to your own calls. Internal documentation supports three things a prospect will care about: Grace Hill has specialized in multifamily mystery shopping for close to four decades; the same shopper is not sent back to the same location inside an 18-month span, which is why shoppers are drawn from surrounding markets to cover thinner ones; and shoppers can be pulled from an assignment or removed from the pool entirely for quality, anonymity, conduct or integrity problems, with removal applied across every Grace Hill shopping platform and any third-party shopper vendor. Say plainly what is not documented: there is no published shopper recruitment, certification or training curriculum in GHU or AdminHQ as of 2026-08-21, so do not describe shoppers as 'certified' or 'trained to a Grace Hill curriculum.' Two real limits to lead with rather than hide: coverage is the continental U.S., and shops complete fastest in large metros — remote or low-shopper-density markets and expensive metros take longer, and route shoppers are used to reach the hard ones. Shops in Nevada are conducted by licensed private investigators because state law requires it.
ms-human-shoppers.proof: FAQ: PerformanceHQ - Mystery Shop | 1623 (GHU) states Grace Hill has specialized in multifamily mystery shopping for nearly 40 years, uses independent contractors nationally, ensures a shopper does not return to the same location in less than 18 months, uses route shoppers for remote/difficult markets, can complete shops throughout the continental U.S. with fastest completion in major metros, and notes Nevada shops are completed by licensed private investigators as dictated by state law. Mystery Shopping: Shopper Exclusions | 8125 (GHU) establishes client-specific and complete exclusion from the independent contractor pool for professional conduct, client risk (including breach of shopper anonymity), quality/reliability (incomplete, inaccurate or unusable reports; failure to follow client instructions), and ethical/compliance grounds (falsification of reports); exclusions are generally permanent and are applied across active Grace Hill mystery shopping platforms and third-party shopper vendors.
ms-human-shoppers.statedLimit: Coverage is the continental U.S.; markets with low shopper density, remote geography, or high cost of living take longer to complete, and Nevada shops must be conducted by licensed private investigators (GHU 1623).

ms-phone.note: Yes. Phone inquiry shops are a standard shop type, sold in both recorded and non-recorded form, and are scored on a standard phone questionnaire. Recorded versions let a manager hear the call instead of debating it. Two limits worth stating up front. First, scope: a phone shop evaluates the call. It does not evaluate follow-up, so follow-up questions cannot be added to a phone shop questionnaire — if follow-up matters, that belongs on an internet or onsite/combo shop. Second, phone number hygiene is the client's job: shoppers make several spaced-out attempts to reach the exact number on file, and if that number rings the wrong business, a corporate line, or a dead line, the shop is documented and scored as a valid zero. Those zeros are not refunded or credited, and Grace Hill does not chase individual bad numbers, so tell customers to audit location names, addresses, phone numbers, touring hours and closures before launch. If a phone shop is recorded, recording consent is the client's responsibility (see the video/recording note).
ms-phone.proof: Product Resources: PerformanceHQ/Validate Shop Templates... | 1060 (GHU) lists a Phone Shop Template among available shop templates. Salesforce Opportunities - Adding Contact Role and Products | 2136 (GHU) shows program bundles built from Phone (Non-recorded) and Phone (Recorded) shop types. Mystery Shop Operations Ticket Resolution Process: Shopping Team | 8130 (GHU) states questionnaire updates must align with Grace Hill's shop-type definitions and gives the example that phone shops do not include evaluation of follow-up, so follow-up questions cannot be added to a phone shop. FAQ: PerformanceHQ - Mystery Shop | 1623 (GHU) documents the bad-phone-number protocol — up to five spaced call attempts to the number listed in the client's account, documented in the shop report, shops going through with a valid score of zero, no refund or credit for inaccurate client-provided information, and that Grace Hill does not notify clients of individual bad numbers. Mystery Shopping Admin Guide | 5000 (AdminHQ) confirms Rush ordering exists for phone non-recorded shops.
ms-phone.statedLimit: A phone shop does not evaluate follow-up and follow-up questions cannot be added to it (GHU 8130); and a shop against a bad client-supplied phone number scores a valid zero that is not due a refund or credit (GHU 1623).

ms-email.note: Yes. Internet inquiry shops submit a lead through the property's own website and grade the response. Set expectations on three documented boundaries. Scope: an internet shop evaluates the email/web response — it does not evaluate a response by telephone, so phone-handling questions cannot be added to an internet shop questionnaire. Targeting: you cannot target a named employee on an internet shop order; whoever answers the lead is who gets evaluated. Setup: the client must supply the website URL used for internet lead submission for each location, or the shop cannot be executed as intended. Upside for the buyer: internet shops are among the fastest-turning types, and each internet question category maps to specific short upskill courses, so a slow or thin email response converts straight into an assignable coaching action.
ms-email.proof: Product Resources: PerformanceHQ/Validate Shop Templates... | 1060 (GHU) lists an Internet Shop Template. Mystery Shop Operations Ticket Resolution Process: Shopping Team | 8130 (GHU) states internet shops do not include evaluation of a response via telephone, so no questions about phone calls can be added to an internet shop. Mystery Shopping Admin Guide | 5000 (AdminHQ) states the Select Employee option is not available for Internet shop orders, and that website URLs for submitting internet shops must be provided in the location information. FAQ: PerformanceHQ - Mystery Shop | 1623 (GHU) gives typical delivery windows in which internet shops sit in the fastest band. Internet Mystery Shop Upskill Training - Content Mapping | 135 (AdminHQ) publishes the upskill training mapped to each internet shop survey question.
ms-email.statedLimit: Internet shops cannot be targeted at a specific employee (AdminHQ 5000) and cannot include phone-handling questions, because an internet shop does not evaluate a telephone response (GHU 8130).

ms-onsite.note: Yes. Onsite tour shops are a standard type, and combination shops — the same shopper calls first and then tours — are available on the recurring quarterly program, on the annual plan, and as one-off orders. Four things to say before a customer discovers them later. One: on the quarterly program there is a firm limit of one onsite shop per location per 90-day period; anything beyond that is ordered separately, and an extra order inside the same quarter can land on the same employee twice. Two: onsite shops take the longest to deliver — typically weeks for a random shop and materially longer for a targeted one — and timing depends on geography, local shopper density, how many shops are stacked on one location, and how recently that location was shopped in person. Three: if a location requires an appointment, flag it — appointment-required locations sit outside the standard 90-day timing window, and that preference can now be stored on the location itself instead of being retyped into every order. Four: shared offices, floating leasing staff and multi-phase communities listed as separate locations need to be reconciled before launch, because the goal is one instance of a shop type per leasing team per quarter and that affects the location count.
ms-onsite.proof: Product Resources: PerformanceHQ/Validate Shop Templates... | 1060 (GHU) lists an Onsite Shop Template and a Phone + Onsite Combo Shop Template. FAQ: PerformanceHQ - Mystery Shop | 1623 (GHU) confirms combo shops on the Quarterly Program, Annual & Save Program and à la carte; states a firm limit of one onsite shop per 90 days on the Quarterly Program with supplemental shops ordered à la carte and the risk of shopping the same employee twice in a quarter; gives typical delivery windows of 10-60 days for non-targeted in-person onsite shops and 30-120 days for targeted in-person shops, dependent on geography, shopper penetration, number of shops at one location and recency; and explains the treatment of shared offices, floating leasing professionals and multi-phase locations. Mystery Shopping Admin Guide | 5000 (AdminHQ) states appointment-required locations are not subject to the standard 90-day program timing window. March 2026 Release Notes (AdminHQ) documents appointment preference stored at the location level for program shops and per-order for on-demand shops.
ms-onsite.statedLimit: On the quarterly program there is a firm limit of one onsite shop per 90 days per location, and in-person onsite shops carry the longest delivery windows of any shop type (GHU 1623).

ms-video.note: Yes — video shops exist as a standard shop type, with a dedicated video questionnaire, and are sold inside at least one standard program bundle alongside internet and recorded phone shops. A prospect can also be given a single complimentary video demo shop, on a location Grace Hill selects, with no guaranteed turnaround and no flow into reporting or upskill training. Correct the old framing on states: video shops are not banned in particular states. The gate is consent. In states requiring all-party consent to record — 14 states: CA, CT, DE, FL, IL, MD, MA, MI, MT, NV, NH, OR, PA, WA (confirmed by Product Marketing, 2026-08-21; GHU 1060 and 1061 carry the correct 14, GHU 1623 still lists 13 and omits Oregon; correction in progress as of 2026-08-21) — the client must have consent in place, and it is the management or ownership company's responsibility to obtain employee authorization, not Grace Hill's. A Grace Hill mystery shopping contract itself carries the consent to provide audio/video recordings; a party without an active shop contract has to give separate written consent first. The one hard stop to know: Grace Hill will not provide audio or video recordings from a location the customer does not own or manage — a competitor shop — in an all-party-consent state. Sample employee and customer consent forms are available.
ms-video.proof: Product Resources: PerformanceHQ/Validate Shop Templates, Sample Shop Reports, Video Tour, Recording Consent Form | 1060 (GHU) lists a Video Shop Template, provides sample onsite audio and video recording samples, and states that customers not under active mystery shop contract must provide separate consent before shops can be recorded in any state requiring 2+ party consent (list given as CA, CT, DE, FL, IL, MD, MA, MI, MT, NV, NH, OR, PA, WA) and that recordings cannot be provided at any non-owned or non-managed location in a 2+ party consent state. Product Resources: Ellis (Legacy platform) Shop Templates... | 1061 (GHU) repeats the same consent condition and explicitly names non-owned/non-managed 'competitor' locations. FAQ: PerformanceHQ - Mystery Shop | 1623 (GHU) states it is the management or ownership company's responsibility to obtain recording authorizations, names 13 two-party-consent states for audio recording (CA, CT, DE, FL, IL, MD, MA, MI, MT, NV, NH, PA, WA) — this list is incomplete: it omits Oregon. Product Marketing confirmed on 2026-08-21 that 14 is correct and that GHU 1060 and 1061 are authoritative on the state list; 1623 is being corrected now, and states Grace Hill does not secure these authorizations but can provide a sample form. Salesforce Opportunities - Adding Contact Role and Products | 2136 (GHU) shows a standard program bundle composed of Internet, Phone (Recorded) and Video. Mystery Shopping Free Video Demo Shop | 3080 (GHU) defines the complimentary demo video shop: standard video questionnaire, cannot be targeted, location selected by Grace Hill, not set up in the platform, does not flow into reporting or remediation training, and no guaranteed turnaround time.
ms-video.statedLimit: Grace Hill will not provide audio or video recordings at any non-owned or non-managed (competitor) location in an all-party-consent state, and does not itself secure employee recording authorizations — that is the client's responsibility (GHU 1060, 1061, 1623). All-party-consent state list is 14 states per GHU 1060 and 1061, confirmed by Product Marketing 2026-08-21.

ms-rubric.note: One standardized rubric and a sampling strategy built for multifamily, so scores compare apples to apples across the portfolio. Two operational details worth knowing: shops run on a 90-day program timing window (locations requiring appointments are exempt), and an admin can adjust a shop's score or the shopped employee, which is stamped with the date and the person who changed it. An adjusted score shows on the employee transcript but not on the shop report itself.
ms-rubric.proof: AdminHQ Policy 5000 (Mystery Shopping Admin Guide) documents the 90-day window, appointment exemption, rush eligibility by shop type, and the Adjustments section with its audit note. Policy 5005 repeats the adjustment behavior for managers.

ms-coaching.note: The shop report names the fix and the fix is a mapped course, not a guess. As of the August 2026 release a single shop question can recommend multiple options — Leasing Boosters and Sparks — surfaced in the Upskill Training tab for the admin to assign. Grace Hill publishes the question-category-to-content mapping for internet, phone and onsite shops, so you can show a prospect exactly which course a given failed question triggers.
ms-coaching.proof: AdminHQ August 2026 release notes (Mystery Shop Upskill Training Recommendations, released August 18, 2026) plus the content mapping guides: Internet 135, Phone 140, Onsite 145.

ms-full-call-analysis.note: No, and keep saying no. Everything Grace Hill documents about mystery shopping is a sampled, ordered evaluation: shops are placed as recurring program orders on a quarterly cadence or as one-off orders, one shop at a time, against a scored questionnaire. Analysis rolls up from those completed shops — question-level and skill-level averages, score rankings by employee and location, and an analytics dashboard with trends by shop type. No product that ingests and scores every inbound call your team takes is described in GHU or AdminHQ as of 2026-08-21. That is conversation intelligence and it is a different category of tool. This is a strength, not an apology: a shop is an unsolicited, standardized, third-party-scored prospect experience that maps to a coaching action, and it is not dependent on your phone system capturing anything. If a prospect genuinely needs 100% call coverage, say it is not what this product does and route the requirement rather than stretching the claim.
ms-full-call-analysis.proof: Mystery Shopping Admin Guide | 5000 and Mystery Shopping Manager Guide | 5005 (AdminHQ) describe the entire program in terms of discrete Program and A La Carte shop orders moving through Ordered, In Progress, Ready For Review, Final Review and Completed, with one survey and one score per shop. Mystery Shopping Question-Level Analysis Report | 5015 (AdminHQ) states the report evaluates performance on shop survey questions and is not an industry benchmark and does not aggregate Grace Hill customer data. FAQ: PerformanceHQ - Mystery Shop | 1623 (GHU) describes program cadence (quarterly, with a firm limit of one onsite shop per 90 days) and à la carte supplementation — i.e., sampling — and no full-call-capture capability. The only conversation-intelligence platform documented anywhere in GHU is Gong | 2047, which is Grace Hill's own internal sales and customer success coaching tool, not a customer-facing product.
ms-full-call-analysis.statedLimit: Mystery shopping is a sampled program — quarterly program orders plus optional à la carte shops, with a firm cap of one onsite shop per location per 90 days on the program (GHU 1623) — not full coverage of team interactions.

ms-benchmarking.note: Partial, and be precise about which half. What you get today is internal benchmarking, and it is good: score ranking reports by employee and by location that show average score across completed shops alongside how much remediation training was assigned and whether it was completed; a question-level and skill-level analysis report that ranks questions and compares any slice — location, position, group, shop type, date range — against your own company average; and an analytics dashboard with score trends by shop type filtered by position, tenure and group. Ranking reports can exclude targeted shops so they do not distort your averages. What you do not get is an industry shop-score benchmark inside PerformanceHQ. Grace Hill's documentation states plainly that the question-level report is not an industry benchmark and does not aggregate Grace Hill customer data, that today's industry shop benchmarking derives only from a legacy program, and that bringing industry benchmarking into PerformanceHQ is a future intention rather than a current feature. Drop the Ellis awards line: no mystery-shop award program is described in GHU or AdminHQ as of 2026-08-21. The documented award program — the Kingsley Excellence Awards, including Top 100 and Elite 5 — is judged on resident and tenant survey satisfaction against the Kingsley Index™, not on shop scores. If a prospect wants third-party industry comparison, that is the survey line's Kingsley Index™, not the shop line.
ms-benchmarking.proof: Mystery Shopping Question-Level Analysis Report | 5015 (AdminHQ) states: 'This report is not an industry benchmark; it does not aggregate Grace Hill customer data,' and notes only a subset of standard questions are mapped to a skill and fully custom questions are not currently supported. Mystery Shopping Admin Guide | 5000 (AdminHQ) describes the Mystery Shopping Score Ranking Report by Employee and by Location as providing internal benchmarks for company performance, and describes the Mystery Shopping Analytics Dashboard trends by shop type with position, tenure and group filters. FAQ: PerformanceHQ - Mystery Shop | 1623 (GHU) states industry benchmarking today is derived from the Legacy Annual & Save Program only, that Grace Hill is planning to include industry benchmarking in PerformanceHQ in the future, and that PerformanceHQ ranking reports let admins filter out targeted shops to build an internal benchmark. Survey – Kingsley Excellence Award | 9562 (GHU) and FAQs - Survey Solution | 1004 (GHU) define the award program's criteria entirely in terms of survey overall-satisfaction scores measured against the Kingsley Index™; no shop-score award criteria appear in either source.
ms-benchmarking.statedLimit: AdminHQ 5015 states the question-level analysis report is not an industry benchmark and does not aggregate Grace Hill customer data; GHU 1623 states industry shop benchmarking is derived from a legacy program only and is a future intention for PerformanceHQ.

vl-diy-capture.note: DIY capture by the onsite team is the core of Realync. Teams record from a phone or desktop in a few clicks and add captions, voiceovers, music and calls to action; content auto-saves to the cloud with a secure audit trail. Clients self-produce videos of units, amenities, maintenance tutorials, resident events and post-tour follow-ups, with a dedicated client success team and on-demand training. If a team has no capacity, Realync Studios is the fallback — and its constraints are the useful thing to know: site visits book four weeks out, each visit needs a minimum of 10 captures, delivery runs about 10 business days after the last recording day, amenities ship as one overview piece by default, and the contractor cannot provide training or support. No published video length or storage cap as of 2026-08-21.
vl-diy-capture.proof: The pre-recorded videos page describes phone and desktop capture and the editing features. GHU Policy 1006 lists the client-created video types. GHU Policy 9050 states the Studios booking lead time, capture minimum, delivery window and the no-training constraint.
vl-diy-capture.statedLimit: Realync Studios: four-week booking, 10-capture minimum per visit, roughly 10 business days to delivery, no training during a visit.

vl-live-tours.note: Live video tours are richer than the old claim implied. An agent runs a tour by phone or desktop screen-share over a secure private link; prospects watch, ask questions and get answers live. Every session is automatically recorded, which is what makes follow-up and coaching work. Agents can share floor plans and drop pre-recorded video into a live tour, and sessions carry WCAG-oriented support including automated closed captions and real-time transcript generation. Live Video Intelligence layers AI over the recording: engagement metrics, agent performance, topic analysis of what drives conversion, and automated coaching insights — also positioned for monitoring Fair Housing and WCAG compliance. Prospects can self-book where a scheduler integration exists. Not published as of 2026-08-21: participant cap, session length cap, or recording retention period — confirm before promising any of them.
vl-live-tours.proof: The live-video-tours page documents screen-share delivery, automatic recording, WCAG support, floor plans, in-session pre-recorded video and Live Video Intelligence. The Realync compliance page documents automated captions and real-time transcripts. The integrations page lists the scheduler partners.
vl-live-tours.statedLimit: No published participant cap, session length cap, or recording retention period as of 2026-08-21.

vl-unit-level.note: Recorded unit-level video is the product's central premise, framed against the finding that 99% of renters want to see the exact unit they will rent. Onsite teams capture individual units from a phone; where Studios captures instead, clients now select the exact units and spaces in-app through Units Overview and Request Studios, a May 2026 release that replaced spreadsheets and email. The practical constraint is inventory freshness rather than capability: a unit video is accurate only until the unit is turned or renovated, and re-capture is a manual client workflow with no published automation. Studios visits also require a 10-capture minimum, and amenities are delivered as a single overview piece unless extra captures are purchased.
vl-unit-level.proof: The virtual leasing page carries the 99% figure. AdminHQ May 2026 release notes document the in-app Studios unit request flow. GHU Policy 9050 sets the capture minimum and the amenity default.
vl-unit-level.statedLimit: Re-capture after a turn or renovation is a manual client workflow; no published automation or refresh cadence.

vl-3d.note: Keep this Partial and be precise about what Realync 3D means. The native offering is 360-degree click-through tours — an interactive choose-your-path video experience where a prospect clicks between rooms. No first-party page states whether the underlying technology is photogrammetry or 360 video, and no dollhouse or measurement view is described as of 2026-08-21. Two more constraints: 360 click-throughs are produced by the Realync Studios team rather than captured DIY, and they consume capture allotment at roughly three hours per ten click-throughs. True 3D comes through the Matterport integration, where Realync videos embed inside a Matterport tour as Mattertags — which implies the customer brings their own Matterport, though the page does not state subscription requirements.
vl-3d.proof: GHU Policy 1006 describes 360 tours as an interactive click-through video tour. The 360-tours page states the expert team handles creation and does not specify the technology. GHU Policy 9050 gives the three-hours-per-ten figure. The Matterport page describes Realync videos embedding as Mattertags.
vl-3d.statedLimit: 360 click-throughs are Studios-produced, not DIY, and consume capture allotment. No native photogrammetry 3D is described; Matterport 3D requires the Matterport platform.

vl-self-guided.note: Partial is correct, and the reason is a common source of confusion in deals. Realync's Virtual Self-Guided Video Tours are a website-embedded widget, positioned like a chatbot, offering choose-your-own-path video so prospects explore independently around the clock. That is self-guided viewing, powered by existing pre-recorded Realync video — not physical self-guided touring. No smart lock, access control, ID verification or on-site entry capability is described on Realync or Grace Hill pages as of 2026-08-21. If a prospect asks about unattended on-site tours, that is a different category needing an access-control partner. Never let 'self-guided' pass unqualified. Stated prerequisite: the tours run on existing video, so a property with no library cannot switch them on.
vl-self-guided.proof: The self-guided page states the tours are embedded into the website similar to a chatbot and powered by Realync pre-recorded videos, and that Studios is not required but pre-recorded video content is.
vl-self-guided.statedLimit: Video-based only; requires an existing pre-recorded library; no physical access control, smart lock or ID verification described as of 2026-08-21.

vl-crm-integration.note: Named CRM integrations: Anyone Home by Inhabit, Entrata, Funnel, Knock and Yardi — letting an agent send video and automatically log the activity inside their existing workflow. Named schedulers for prospect self-booking of live tours: Anyone Home by Inhabit and Hyly.ai. Realync also publishes per-integration explainers for Yardi, Entrata, Knock, BetterBot, Engrain, Matterport and Apartments.com, and Grace Hill's FAQ adds that Realync integrates through an open API and ongoing partnership work. Two honest qualifiers: the page's own fallback is that any system supporting an embed code or video link can display Realync video, and unlisted platforms require a custom integration request — so embed-level display is not the same as native activity logging. No field mapping or two-way sync specification is published as of 2026-08-21.
vl-crm-integration.proof: The integrations page names the CRM and scheduler partners and states video activity is automatically logged, and carries the embed-code fallback and custom-integration request language. GHU Policy 1006 states the open API.
vl-crm-integration.statedLimit: Unlisted platforms are embed-code display or a custom-integration request, not a native integration. No published field mapping or sync depth.

vl-analytics.note: Engagement analytics are confirmed at two levels. The dashboard tracks video views, prospect engagement and leasing team performance in real time, showing which videos drive engagement and what viewers did. Grace Hill's Realync FAQ is more specific on the metric set: views, signed leases, qualifying leads, clicks, engagement rates and conversion statistics. Live Video Intelligence adds AI analysis of live tours — engagement scoring, agent performance, topic analysis of what drives conversion, automated coaching insights — and is positioned for monitoring Fair Housing and WCAG compliance. Four things are not published as of 2026-08-21: the full metric dictionary, the reporting hierarchy across property, region and portfolio, the attribution window for a signed lease credited to a video, and the data retention period. Those are exactly what a sophisticated buyer asks, so promise a written answer rather than improvising one.
vl-analytics.proof: The analytics dashboard page documents the real-time metrics and Live Video Intelligence. GHU Policy 1006 lists the metric set. The live tours page lists topic analysis and coaching.
vl-analytics.statedLimit: No published metric dictionary, reporting hierarchy, lease-attribution window or data retention policy as of 2026-08-21.

vl-syndication.note: Content syndication is confirmed with a named partner list: Anyone Home by Inhabit, Entrata, BetterBot, Conversion Logix, EliseAI, Engrain, G5, Hyly.ai, Jonah, PERQ, PowerPro, Pynwheel, RealPage, Rent.com, RentCafe, Repli and Zillow. Be careful with the language: the true ILS and marketplace destinations in that list are Zillow, Rent.com, RentCafe and RealPage, plus a published Apartments.com integration. The rest are chatbots, websites, tour scheduling, site-map and marketing-automation platforms — accurate to call them syndication destinations, inaccurate to call them ILSs. One nuance: the page's fallback is that any system supporting an embed code or video link can showcase Realync video, so some destinations are display-by-embed rather than a managed feed. No per-ILS field mapping, feed cadence, or guarantee that a given ILS renders 360 or live-tour content is published.
vl-syndication.proof: The integrations page names all seventeen syndication partners and states video distributes across apartment search and leasing platforms, and carries the embed-code fallback and custom-integration language.
vl-syndication.statedLimit: Some destinations are embed-code display rather than a managed feed; no published feed cadence or per-ILS rendering guarantee.

md-rent-comps.note: Automated unit-level rent comparables in any US market from a single address. Comp selection is modeled: submarket, unit size, property age, stories, 200+ building and unit amenities, plus computer-vision quality scoring of listing photos. HelloData® publishes two accuracy figures — comps align with property manager comp selections 9 times out of 10, and a 97% match with actual rent rolls. Say the number, then say it is vendor-published with no methodology or date attached. Do not present it as audited. In PerformanceHQ, rent comps surface in the Dashboard HelloData® widget and in Intelligence+ and Ask Gracie™, both of which require an active HelloData® subscription.
md-rent-comps.proof: The homepage states automated rent comps with unit-level pricing and the 97% match figure; the comp-detection help article states the 9-out-of-10 alignment. AdminHQ Policy 2040 documents the widget; Policy 6010 states the subscription requirement.
md-rent-comps.statedLimit: Comp selection is a model, not a survey; both accuracy figures are undated and carry no published methodology.

md-concessions.note: Concession tracking is real and unusually well documented. HelloData® extracts specials from property-website banners using AI, including concessions advertised inside images. The API exposes concessions_history with structured free months or weeks, dollar amounts, fee waivers and lease-term conditions, plus a special_included flag showing whether a concession was already in the asking price. Net effective rent amortizes one-time discounts across the lease term, defaulting to 12 months unless the offer says otherwise. The honest limit: only publicly advertised concessions are captured. Unadvertised, negotiated or agent-discretion concessions are not observable, so net effective rent is a floor on generosity rather than a complete picture.
md-concessions.proof: The homepage describes capturing specials banners and the 12-month amortization default. The API changelog adds visual and image concession detection and the special_included field. AdminHQ Policy 2040 lists average concession percentages in the widget.
md-concessions.statedLimit: Only publicly advertised concessions are captured; the 12-month amortization is a default assumption.

md-coverage.note: Do not quote a single coverage number. Five HelloData® pages disagree, all live on 2026-08-21: the homepage says 38.5M+ units surveyed daily from over 250,000 property websites, a help article says over 35 million updated every 24 hours, the API product page says over 25M units and 4M+ properties daily, and two help articles say 2.2 million apartment buildings comprising roughly 23.1 million units. None carries an 'as of' date and the homepage footer still reads 2025. Safest rep language: tens of millions of US units, refreshed daily — HelloData® publishes figures between 23 million and 38.5 million depending on the page, and I will confirm the current number in writing. Also note market search is optimized for metropolitan areas, so rural coverage returns fewer results.
md-coverage.proof: Homepage states 38.5M+ units and 250,000+ property websites. The which-markets help article states 2.2 million buildings and approximately 23.1 million units. The what-apartment-data help article states over 35 million nationwide every 24 hours. The APIs page states over 25M units and 4M+ properties every day. All retrieved 2026-08-21; none dated.
md-coverage.statedLimit: Four conflicting first-party unit counts as of 2026-08-21, none dated. Market search is optimized for metro areas.

md-api.note: A real versioned REST API exists at docs.hellodata.ai. The commercial point matters most: API access sits on HelloData®'s own Portfolio tier, and no page states that a PerformanceHQ seat includes it. AdminHQ confirms Intelligence+ market intelligence requires an active HelloData® subscription. Treat the API as a separate HelloData® contract until product says otherwise, and do not quote a per-call price — the pricing page and a help article disagree ($0.10 versus $0.50).

md-submarket.note: Submarket analysis is supported as user-drawn geography rather than a fixed taxonomy. Map-based trend analysis and development feasibility with custom survey regions are advertised, and comp detection uses submarket location as an input. In the API, market-search takes GeoJSON-style polygons including shapes with holes and multiple disconnected areas, and a shape-search endpoint exists. No built-in market, submarket or ZIP boundary set is documented as of 2026-08-21, so the customer defines the region. Two limits to volunteer: each market-search request is capped at 2,500 properties, and searches are optimized for metropolitan areas with fewer results in rural markets. Filters include year built, unit count, stories, unit mix, amenities, listing status, and student, senior and affordable flags.

md-availability.note: Partial is right and the documentation explains why. The API returns building_availability and availability_periods with enter-market and exit-market dates, price-plan history, deposits, lease term and days-on-market — so availability is observed from what competitors publish on their own websites, refreshed daily. That is advertised availability, not a competitor's actual vacancy: units held offline, pre-leased but still posted, or never posted will not reconcile with a rent roll. Two occupancy fields are marked deprecated in the changelog — occupancy_over_time, which states it will be removed in future versions, and estimated_occupancy — so do not build a pitch on modeled occupancy. Never say real-time. Say daily-refreshed observed availability and days-on-market from public listings.

The changelog deprecates estimated_occupancy. AdminHQ Policy 2040 lists leased and active unit counts and average days on market in the PerformanceHQ widget.

tr-content-types.note: Content types are deliberately different, not interchangeable, and policy says so: a foundational compliance course, a Spark, an In the Know, a maintenance demonstration, an assessment and a reinforcement activity are not meant to use the same instructional approach. Position by what the learner needs to do. A full course is for foundational knowledge that has to hold up under scrutiny. Sparks are 2-to-5-minute microlearning for just-in-time reinforcement — 175+ of them. Leading Edge of Maintenance is short-form trade demonstration, 100+. Boosters are short skill lifts, 50+, and they are what a failed Mystery Shop question maps to. In the Know is supplemental and is how a regulatory development gets covered fast without waiting for a course revision. Refreshers re-cover a topic without re-running the full course. Never sell a Spark as a compliance course or a course as microlearning — the whole point is that the format follows the job.

po-review-approval.note: Policy changes route through governance inside the platform, not email. A draft revision goes to named reviewers who comment and suggest, then to named approvers who approve or reject with comments, invitations included. Approvers can comment but cannot edit the text, which keeps the two roles clean, and the workflow keeps an auditable record of the policy lifecycle. One expectation to set: if the content changes mid-approval, all completed approvals must be deleted and resent.

po-substitution-variables.note: A job title, brand name or department is stored as a substitution variable and managed centrally. Update the value once and every policy using it reflects it, with a preview showing either labels or real values. Manual section headers are themselves variables. For audit purposes the variables are versioned, so the system can show which value was in effect when a policy was viewed at a past date — and by design they cannot be deleted, deliberately, to preserve historical integrity. This is the strongest audit answer in the product.

po-version-restore.note: Any inactive revision can be restored as a new draft, carrying its content, attachments and policy links intact, then edited and published normally. Content Vault references in the restored text repoint to current versions automatically. Nothing is lost: every revision ever published stays in history, and restoring an old one does not delete anything published after it. The option is unavailable while an active pending revision exists.

po-manual-scope.note: Access is controlled at two levels. A manual's Scope setting decides whether all employees see it or only those an admin selects. Each policy also has a visibility status — Hidden removes it for basic users and drops it out of Ask Gracie™'s answers while admins keep working on it. The Manuals page shows visible and hidden counts per manual, and a manual's whole active revision can be printed or exported. This is how a customer stages a rollout or keeps a region-specific manual off everyone else's screen.

po-implementation.note: Two ways to go live, and quote the right one. Standard gives the policies in the selected package plus the editing tools and launch resources — typically 21 to 30 days. Customized is hands-on: Grace Hill reviews the customer's existing policies, suggests edits against current regulation and best practice, and meets stakeholders to align policies to their processes — averaging about 18 weeks, moving with content complexity and stakeholder availability. Quoting 21 to 30 days for a customized build is how an implementation starts behind.

sv-survey-logic.note: Surveys adapt to the respondent three ways. Display Logic shows or hides a question based on a previous answer or a location attribute. Skip Logic jumps a respondent forward. Branching controls which whole pages they see. They combine, previews reflect the logic, and a completed transcript shows only what that respondent actually saw. Limits to state: skip logic only moves forward and only within a page or to end of page or survey, so cross-page routing needs branching; location-based display logic cannot be previewed because there is no location context; logic rules are dropped automatically if the referenced question is deleted or reordered above the dependent one; and because different respondents see different questions, per-question response counts and completion rates vary — which matters when reading results. Customer configures it on Ad Hoc and Pulse; we configure it on Annual and Moments That Matter.
sv-survey-logic.proof: AdminHQ Policy 6008, Survey Logic, defines the three types and every limit above. Policy 6000 states who configures which.

sv-anonymous.note: Anonymous Surveys collect feedback with no login, no authentication and no personally identifiable information, distributed by public link or QR code — built for lobby kiosks, posters and on-site feedback stations. Be explicit about the trade-off, because it is what a rep gets caught on: you get aggregate scores, response counts and question-level breakdowns, plus location filtering only if the QR codes carried location data. You do not get individual respondent records, row-level export, or names and emails. Results also stay hidden until a minimum response threshold is met, and that applies to every filtered view, so thin slices look empty. Full anonymity also depends on how the survey is designed, so a customer promising absolute anonymity should have the questionnaire reviewed.
sv-anonymous.proof: AdminHQ Policy 6007 states the no-login, no-PII design, exactly what is and is not available in reporting, and the minimum-response threshold across all filters. The May 2026 release notes state full anonymity depends on survey design and data collected.

sv-benchmark-integrity.note: Comparability is protected deliberately, and it is worth saying out loud because a competitor cannot claim it. Three mechanisms: benchmark instruments keep dedicated distribution methodologies so delivery does not drift and break the benchmark — anonymous open distribution is reserved for the occupant survey, which has its own; benchmark questions cannot be edited by the customer; and during questionnaire review our practice is to defend the existing question set specifically so the customer keeps both the Kingsley Index™ comparison and the year-over-year trend. Scores are always segmented by property type and there is a benchmark value for every individual question, so a score is compared like-for-like rather than against a blended average.
sv-benchmark-integrity.proof: AdminHQ May 2026 release notes state benchmark instruments maintain dedicated distribution methodologies to preserve benchmark integrity. GHU Policy 1619 states benchmark questions cannot be changed. GHU Policy 9521 states the advocacy practice. GHU Policy 9511 states the per-question benchmark and property-type segmentation.

sv-sms.note: Surveys go out by email, and SMS can be added as a second channel with a unique link the respondent taps to complete in their mobile browser. Two limits to carry: email stays the default and cannot be removed from a send; and SMS is currently available for Resident Annual, Moments That Matter and Employee surveys, is set up by Grace Hill rather than self-served, and adding it to an existing Moments That Matter program requires the Design Team to rebuild those surveys. SMS content is deliberately plain — no images, styling or extra links — for compliance and deliverability.

Any international program including Canada is classified high complexity for implementation.

ms-scoring-and-score-adjustment.note: A shop score is a percentage: points earned on the questionnaire against points available, with each question carrying a point value that reflects how much that behavior matters. Every question also rolls up to a skill, which is what drives the question-level and skill-level analysis. The part customers love once they hear it: the score is not final. Once a shop reaches Ready For Review, an admin or a manager over that employee can override the employee named on the shop and enter an adjusted score, add comments visible only to reviewers, and the system stamps who changed what and when. Two limits to state: the adjusted score field does not accept decimals, and the adjusted score shows on the employee's transcript but is not currently reflected on the shop report document itself. There is also a formal dispute path if you think the shopper got it wrong, including rescoring or arranging a replacement shop. And once a shop is completed via Skip Assignments & Complete Shop, that cannot be undone and employee and comment edits close — though the score can still be changed at any time.

ms-shop-to-course-mapping.note: This is the differentiator most reps under-sell. Every standard shop question is mapped to specific short courses — Leasing Boosters and Sparks — so a low score produces named, assignable coaching rather than a vague debrief. As of the August 2026 release a single shop question can recommend more than one course, and the published mappings for internet, phone and onsite shops are available so a customer can see exactly which course follows which miss. When a Leasing Booster is assigned, the employee is prompted after the course to reflect on their shop result and write an improvement plan, and that plan lands on their completion certificate. Deliberate design choice to explain, not defend: training is never auto-assigned. A manager reviews the shop with the employee first, then chooses what to assign and sets the days to complete — because if a manager adjusts a score, auto-assigning the course tied to that question would confuse the employee. Training subscribers can also assign anything else in their catalog. Two limits: questions a customer adds or deletes do not carry upskill mappings, and some standard questions have no mapped training.

ms-ordering-and-turnaround.note: Set the operating rhythm before signature. Program shops run on a 90-day cadence and the order carries a program range with a start and end date; admins can also bulk-order one-off shops by selecting all locations, a group or a region, add a second shop to a location already on the order, target a named employee (with required shopper notes), flag appointment-required, or mark a shop Rush. Rush is only available on phone non-recorded and onsite non-recorded shops, it carries an additional fee, it buys priority scheduling and quality-control review, and it does not come with a guaranteed delivery date. Typical delivery: internet, phone and virtual shops land fastest, in-person onsite shops take longest, and targeting stretches every window. Now the parts that bite: one-off shops cannot be cancelled once ordered; a program shop can only be cancelled if the location is being sold, the request reaches Grace Hill before the 25th of the month preceding the program period, and the location is also set inactive; and questionnaire or program location changes only apply to upcoming quarters and must be submitted well before the quarter starts. Shop reports are not visible until the shop reaches Ready For Review, and a daily digest email alert can notify reviewers as shops arrive.

ms-questionnaire-customization.note: Customers can shape what gets scored: rewrite shopper instructions to match their standards, delete questions that do not matter to them, add their own, and re-weight points to reflect what they actually care about in the customer experience. Four rules to state plainly so nobody is surprised. Benchmark-designated questions stay in the questionnaire even if a customer zeroes out their point values. Added or deleted questions drop out of the upskill training recommendations, and fully custom questions are not currently supported in the question-level analysis report. Changes only take effect for upcoming quarters and must be submitted well ahead of the quarter start. And changes must respect what each shop type actually evaluates — you cannot add follow-up questions to a phone shop or phone-handling questions to an internet shop. Heavier customization goes through a Grace Hill approval step. Special housing types are supported — student, senior, military, affordable — but the customer has to flag them in their location notes or shoppers will treat the property as conventional market-rate, and the shopper will not necessarily match the resident demographic; they present a plausible scenario instead.
ms-questionnaire-customization.proof: FAQ: PerformanceHQ - Mystery Shop | 1623 (GHU) lists permitted questionnaire modifications (added shopper instruction, deleting questions, adding questions, modifying scores) with the notes that deleted and added questions do not result in upskill training recommendations and that Benchmark-designated questions must be left intact even if point values are removed; it also documents support for student, senior, military and affordable housing with the requirement that the client note this in location comments and that the shopper will present an eligible-resident scenario rather than necessarily matching the demographic. Mystery Shop Operations Ticket Resolution Process: Shopping Team | 8130 (GHU) requires questionnaire updates to be received well before quarter commencement and to align with Grace Hill's shop-type definitions. Shop Program Implementation Process | 8105 (GHU) requires escalation for approval when customization exceeds a defined number of questions. Mystery Shopping Question-Level Analysis Report | 5015 (AdminHQ) states only a subset of standard questions are mapped to a skill and that non-standard fully custom questions are not currently supported in that report.

rm-listings-social-and-lbv.note: Reputation Management is wider than reviews, and the extra modules often close the deal. Listings: one place to see how accurate each property's information is across third-party sites, catch mismatched addresses, phone numbers and hours, spot missing, duplicate or error listings, correct them directly, and schedule automated updates so data does not drift. Social: a consolidated feed of posts across connected accounts, plus a publishing calendar with a real approval workflow — pending approval, scheduled, rejected, errors, published — and permissions so some users post directly while others need admin sign-off. Benchmarking: the Local Brand Visibility score, which unlike a pure star-rating average combines reviews, social engagement, online listings, search rankings and local competitors into a single comparative number, alongside SEO rankings and the search terms prospects actually use to find your properties. Positioning line that is accurate: LBV benchmarks your local brand presence against nearby competitors; the Kingsley Index™ benchmarks resident and tenant satisfaction across the industry — customers on both get both lenses. Caveat: module availability varies by package tier, so confirm the tier before demoing a module.
rm-listings-social-and-lbv.proof: Reputation Management | 8000 (AdminHQ) documents Listings Management (Listings Accuracy, Listings Summary, Listings Optimization with direct correction, Missing/Duplicate/Error Listings, Locations, Scheduled Updates), Social Media Management (Summary, Feed, Publish with Calendar, Pending Approval, Scheduled, Rejected, Errors, Published, and permissions for direct publishing versus admin approval), and Analytics & Reporting including the LBV Score benchmark tracking reviews, social media activity, online listings and search rankings with local-competitor comparison, plus SEO Rankings and Search Insights. FAQs - Reputation Management Solution | 1005 (GHU) states the LBV score lets multifamily organizations compare their online presence with local and regional competitors, that unlike scoring methods focused solely on review ratings it combines reviews, social media engagement, local competitors, online listings and search rankings, and that clients gain better benchmarking visibility by using both the Kingsley Index and the LBV score. GTM: Reputation Management | 1607 (GHU) confirms three packages, so module availability is tier-dependent.

tr-refresher-strategy.note: Annual compliance refreshers were redesigned for 2026 off customer feedback. They release quarterly to spread compliance touchpoints and cut learner fatigue, each opens with a short scenario-based pre-check so learners who demonstrate mastery skip what they already know and still get full completion credit while others are routed to short targeted explanations, and each carries a required trending-topic module so the content stays current. One limit: the pre-check is core to the design and cannot be disabled at client level.

tr-pathways.note: A template system for standardized onboarding and remediation journeys, distinct from learning plans. Admins build reusable task-and-rule templates for a job function, location or department, assign by individual, position, location or group, and edit a live template to improve future journeys without disrupting people already in flight. If the employee on a pathway changes, progress resets and the new assignee's existing training records are verified. Rule-based start dates follow the organization's hire-date or created-date setting; individually assigned pathways appear immediately.
tr-pathways.proof: AdminHQ April 2026 release notes describe the template library, dynamic assignment, reset with record verification, and editing active templates. AdminHQ Policy 11 documents the start-date behaviour.

tr-partner-content.note: Beyond Grace Hill courseware the catalog carries partner content, filterable by provider so a prospect sees exactly what comes from where — which matters in maintenance and technical skills conversations. Behavioural limits to know before promising anything: some partner content is delivered in the partner's own mobile app rather than our course player, one partner's courses can only be assigned as a curated learning plan rather than individually, and those assignments cannot be set to recur or completed a second time.
tr-partner-content.proof: GHU Policy 7001 documents the content-provider filter covering Grace Hill, Interplay Learning, Leap, Realync and SkillCat. AdminHQ Policy 3070 states SkillCat courses are not eligible for direct assignment and those learning plans cannot recur.

md-expense-benchmarks.note: A distinct capability from rent comps and not previously on the sheet. HelloData® publishes Year-1 operating expense benchmarks drawn from more than 25,000 US multifamily properties, with an advertised under-10% median error, exposed through a documented expense-benchmarks API endpoint. The error figure carries no publication date, so present it as vendor-published rather than audited.
md-expense-benchmarks.proof: The homepage states operating expense benchmarks with under 10% median error. The which-markets help article states the expense comps database covers more than 25,000 multifamily properties. The API reference lists the expense-benchmarks endpoint.

vl-live-video-intelligence.note: An AI layer over recorded live tours: engagement scoring, agent performance data, topic analysis of what drives conversion, and automated coaching insights. Also positioned for monitoring Fair Housing and WCAG compliance across virtual tours. A differentiator that was not represented in the claim set at all — and the compliance angle is the half most likely to matter to a risk-conscious buyer.
vl-live-video-intelligence.proof: The live-video-tours and analytics-dashboard pages describe the engagement metrics, topic analysis, coaching insights and Fair Housing and WCAG monitoring. AdminHQ March 2026 release notes list the Live Video Intelligence solution preview.

vl-studios-slas.note: The most-asked operational questions have documented answers: site visits book four weeks out, each visit needs a minimum of 10 captures counting Realync videos and 360 click-throughs, on-site time runs roughly three hours per ten captures, content reaches the property's account about 10 business days after the last recording day, amenities ship as one overview piece by default, and the contractor cannot provide training or troubleshooting. Clients now select units in-app through Units Overview and Request Studios.
vl-studios-slas.proof: GHU Policy 9050, Realync Studios Overview, states each standard. AdminHQ May 2026 release notes document the in-app request flow.

po-ai-content-question.note: Yes, and this is the stronger half of the search story. Ask Gracie™ answers plain-language questions about policy content: she prioritizes the company's own policies and custom content over general Grace Hill courseware, carries source chips linking straight to the specific policy she used, holds session context across a conversation, and restricts answers to content that person is authorized to see. Three gates a rep must know before demoing: policy access is an admin toggle under Feature Settings, the Hide Gracie Chatbot setting is active by default so enabling it is an admin action, and a Hidden policy never appears in her answers. ai-data-boundary.note: Partial, and this is the one to get right because the instinctive claim is wrong. For the Gracie assistant across Policies and Training, answers do come from the customer's own content plus Grace Hill courseware, with authorization respected. For Ask Gracie™ inside Intelligence+ the boundary is different: she is scoped to portfolio data and answers on survey and resident feedback, property rankings, training compliance and executive summaries — but market intelligence comes from HelloData® market comps, which is external market data, not the customer's approved content. So never say "pulls only from your own approved content" about Intelligence+. The accurate version is better anyway: your data, plus market data you would otherwise buy separately. Competitor values on this row are not yet researched — treat blanks as Unknown, not as a No.
ai-data-boundary.proof: AdminHQ Policy 6010 lists the Ask Gracie™ topics and states market intelligence is sourced from HelloData® and requires an active subscription. AdminHQ Policy 2125 documents the Gracie assistant's content scope and Smart Access Control.
ai-data-boundary.statedLimit: Intelligence+ Ask Gracie™ draws on HelloData® market comps as well as customer data, so 'only your own approved content' is inaccurate there. Chat history is not saved, time-trend queries and overdue-assignment data are not yet supported, and answer export is a future update.
